name: Jasper
tagline: One of the original AI copywriting platforms, now built for brand-consistent marketing content at scale.
tldr: Jasper (formerly Jarvis / Conversion.ai) is an AI writing platform built for marketing teams, offering brand voice, knowledge assets, and templates for blog, ad, and social copy.
Best for marketing teams and businesses that need repeatable, on-brand content across many formats rather than solo one-off writing.
Was one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies ever pre-ChatGPT, reportedly reaching $45M ARR in about 12 months before general-purpose chatbots reshaped the AI-writing market.
Simplified its pricing in 2026 down to two core plans (Pro and Business), discontinuing the older Creator tier and migrating existing Creator users to Pro at a higher price.
Positioned as a professional-grade tool for teams needing brand consistency, but reviewers note it still requires human editing and supervision.

pricing.model: Subscription, no free tier (7-day free trial)

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: 1 user seat (expandable), Canvas, 2 Brand Voices, 5 Knowledge assets, 3 Audiences, Jasper Chat, AI Image Suite; replaced the older Creator tier in 2026

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: Unlimited Brand Voices/Knowledge/Audiences, Jasper Agents, AI App Builder (Studio), API access, SSO, dedicated account manager

pros: Brand Voice and Knowledge Base features help keep output consistent across a marketing team
Wide library of templates covering blog, ad, and social copy speeds up routine content production
Long track record and enterprise customer base gives it credibility for larger marketing orgs
Jasper Chat and AI Image Suite bundle text and basic image generation in one subscription
cons: No free tier: users must commit to a paid plan (after a 7-day trial) to use the product at all
2026 pricing restructure discontinued the cheaper Creator tier, raising costs for existing lower-tier subscribers
Output still requires meaningful human editing; some reviewers describe it as a 'sophisticated' starting draft rather than finished copy
Business-tier pricing is opaque (custom quote only), making cost comparison harder for larger teams

sentiment.quote: Gives many outputs with little information given. The outputs sound like a human wrote them, even though it's through a AI system.
I like to use it because I can produce blog posts, articles, social media posts very safely and efficiently.
An expensive interface for products and services you can get considerably cheaper (even free) elsewhere.

bestFor: Marketing teams needing consistent brand voice across many writers
Agencies producing high-volume, repeatable content formats (blogs, ads, social)
Businesses that want AI writing bundled with basic image generation
Teams that can commit to a paid seat-based plan rather than needing a free tier
hotTake: Jasper once scaled from zero to $45M ARR in about a year, but its 2026 pricing overhaul killed the budget Creator tier and pushed everyone onto a $59+/mo Pro plan.
